item.title: US Embassy in UAE urges citizens exercise ‘heightened vigilance’ in the Middle East
item.description:
US Embassy in UAE urges citizens exercise ‘heightened vigilance’ in the Middle East

The US Embassy in UAE issued a security alert warning its citizens in the Middle East to "exercise heightened vigilance" amid escalations in the region. 

"Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment. Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," it said in its statement. 

It referenced Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, adding that "hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area".

"Americans traveling to or from the Middle East should monitor information about airport and airline operations and develop contingency plans in advance.

"Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions."

item.title: Iran's Araghchi says US-Iran negotiations are not over
item.description:
Iran's Araghchi says US-Iran negotiations are not over

At a diplomatic summit in Baghdad on Sunday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within six days remains on the table, with US-Iran talks set to resume on the seventh day if Washington accepts its conditions. 

The proposal comes amid escalating attacks around the strategic waterway and mounting tensions over US sanctions and a blockade of Iranian ports.

item.title: Israel’s 2026 election: Who are the main leaders and where do they stand on the key issues?
item.description:
Israel’s 2026 election: Who are the main leaders and where do they stand on the key issues?

The Israeli election on 27 October is one of the most important in the country’s history, the first since 2022 and the Hamas-led attacks of 2023, the genocide in Gaza and the war on Iran.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier and now seeking a seventh term, faces wide criticism for his handling of the wars, which have isolated Israel internationally.

Other issues facing Israelis include the security of the occupied West Bank, including the growth of settlements, and compulsory military conscription for ultra-Orthodox communities. 

Middle East Eye takes a look at the main candidates and their parties.

Read more: Israel’s 2026 election: Who are the main leaders and where do they stand on the key issues?

item.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
item.description:
Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next

A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.

Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene.

item.title: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains
item.description:
United Arab Emirates will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces as gains by Iran-backed Houthi fighters alarm Gulf state rulers

  • Yemen civil war: what sparked latest escalation and who is involved?

The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force.

The new cooperation agreement is the first tangible sign that the deep rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is starting to be healed – if only because the advance by Houthi forces across Yemen has alarmed all the rival Gulf state rulers.
